title: Site hub
description: Site icon + name affordance pinned to the top of the navigation sidebar.

documentation.purpose: Branded header at the top of the navigation sidebar. Renders site icon (linked to the dashboard URL) + site title (linked to the home URL, opens in new tab) + a command-palette toggle. Site icon resolves in priority order: `styles.branding.*` cascade logo → REST `site_icon_url` (Settings → General) → default WordPress mark. Site title comes from `useEntityRecord('root', 'site').record.title` with HTML-entity decoding and a window-global fallback.

reads.purpose: Site title (decoded via `decodeEntities` from `@wordpress/html-entities`) + URL fallback for site-without-title case.
Home URL for the site-title anchor (`home`) and the REST Site Icon fallback when no branding logo is configured (`site_icon_url`). Mirrors edit-site SiteHub/SiteIcon.
Branded site icon — branding object read from the resolved admin.json tree via `useKernel()` and passed to SiteIcon helper. Takes precedence over the REST `site_icon_url`.
Fallback for site title before core-data hydrates.
Prefix for a plugin-relative `branding.logo` path so the bundled site icon resolves against the plugin's asset URL (SiteIcon helper). Absolute and protocol-relative logos skip this.
Anchor href for the site-icon button (dashboard); fallback href for the site-title button (home, new tab) when `root/__unstableBase.home` has not resolved.

states.when: Always (renders with whatever data is available; falls back gracefully)
states.renders: Site icon + title + command-palette icon button. Title falls back to filterURLForDisplay(site.url) when title is empty but URL is set.

states.when: No branding logo configured AND `root/__unstableBase` not yet resolved
states.renders: An empty sized placeholder for the icon (no fallback-mark flash) until `site_icon_url` resolves or is confirmed absent.
Site-icon container drops its background — useful when the engine's chrome already provides the surface.

interactions.effect: Open `window.wpAdminShell.homeUrl` in a new tab via native `<a href target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">`.

a11y.focus-management: All three controls (icon, title, palette toggle) are native focusable elements.

keyboard.action: Surfaced as the keyboard shortcut hint on the palette button (`displayShortcut.primary('k')`). The actual binding is shell-level — declared in admin.json's `bindings` block + wired through `useCommandLoader`.

a11y.screen-reader: Site icon button has `aria-label="Go to the Dashboard"`. Title button includes a visually-hidden `(opens in a new tab)` hint inside the link. Palette button has `aria-label="Open command palette"` + `ariaKeyShortcut="Meta+K"`.

constraints.note: Read title via `useEntityRecord('root','site').record.title` (with `decodeEntities`). Falls back to `window.wpAdminShell?.siteName` only as last resort. Fixes a prior bug where the toolbar showed a stale title on first paint.
Wrapped in `memo + forwardRef` because engines may attach refs (e.g. for measure-on-mount layout).

Title button uses the `display: flex; min-width: 0;` wrapper pattern + button-level `flex-grow: 1; min-width: 0; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap` so long site titles truncate cleanly in a constrained sidebar.
Site-icon button + site-title button + palette button all use `render={<a href={...}/>}` so native HTML link behavior works (middle-click new tab, etc.).

WP-admin ships an unlayered `a { color: var(--wp-admin-theme-color) }`. The bundled `core:default` engine ships an unlayered `.wp-admin-shell-site-hub a { color: var(--wpds-color-fg-interactive-neutral) }` rule (+ `:hover/:focus/:active` variants). A non-WPDS engine MUST emit an equivalent rule scoped to this app's chrome surface.
`@wordpress/icons` SVGs lack `fill`. The bundled `core:default` engine forces `.wp-admin-shell-site-hub svg { fill: currentColor }`. A non-WPDS engine MUST do the same for icons it ships.

`@wordpress/ui` Stack flex rules live in `@layer wp-ui-components` and lose to unlayered WP-admin CSS. The bundled `core:default` engine ships an unlayered `[class*="__stack"] { display: flex }` defensive rule. A rebuild using Stack-style flex must defeat unlayered host CSS the same way.

design-system-leakage.purpose: Three controls + layout primitives + visually-hidden `(opens in a new tab)` hint.
Default WordPress-mark fallback icon (SiteIcon helper) when no branding logo or REST `site_icon_url` is set.
Format the `Mod+K` shortcut hint for the palette button.
Compact-URL fallback when site title is empty.
